questions.qtext:
Consider the following logical arguments.

$M$) Hypotheses: If there is gas in the car, then I will go to the store. If I go to the store, then I will get a soda. There is gas in the car. Conclusion: I will get a soda.

$N$) Hypotheses: When Prof. P. gets angry, he fails his entire class. When the entire class fails, the Chancellor gets complaints. When the Chancellor gets complaints, she will either fire Prof. P., cut his salary, or do both. Prof. P. got angry, and he was not fired. Conclusion: Prof. P.'s salary was cut.


Which of the following is TRUE?

options.text: $M$ is correct but $N$ is not a valid argument.
$M$ is not correct but $N$ is a valid argument.

$$
\neg \exists x(P(x)) \wedge \forall x P(x)
$$
